title: Brigginshaw's NRLW legend remains eternal

Brigginshaw's NRLW legend remains eternal

Ali Brigginshaw's decorated rugby league career ended with a heavy defeat but there can be no doubt about the impact the Broncos playmaker has had on the game.

By Nick Campton

Topic:NRL Women’s Premiership

Brigginshaw's final NRLW game ended in a heavy defeat.  (Getty Images: Cameron Spencer)

As the merciless Roosters ran away with the NRLW grand final it was hard to think of a less fitting end for a career as legendary as Ali Brigginshaw's.

The 36-year old and the rest of the Broncos were helpless to stop a Tricolour massacre that ended 30-6 as the Roosters earned a manner of vengeance for last year's grand final defeat to complete a perfect season.

It was over by half-time because Brisbane did not pick up their guns, let alone fire a shot.

The 2026 Sydney Roosters NRLW side has cemented its legacy with a crushing grand final win over the Brisbane Broncos. Here are the quick hits from the NRLW grand final.

They completed just three sets in the entire first half as they drowned under a sea of Roosters points.

From the 15th minute to the 34th minute they only touched the ball to kick it off, drop it or be driven back into the in-goal.

For almost 20 minutes they did not play the ball once, with the Roosters running in six straight tries and between the 15th and 39th minutes they did not complete a set.

All of the weapons that have made Brigginshaw great — her skill, her guile, her cunning and class as a playmaker, which she has carried through her 17 years at the top of women's rugby league — were blunted before she even got a chance to use them.

She did manage to sneak through for a line-break in the second half, a 35 minutes of football that felt like it only happened because it had to happen so we could get to the end, as she held up a pass before hitting a gap with exquisite timing, but had no support.

In the end, her last day was destroyed by a monster of a team who are without question the best NRLW side ever assembled.

They are the culmination of a transformation in women's rugby league that Brigginshaw herself helped bring about through a career that stretches all the way back to the primordial days of women's rugby league.

Brigginshaw's Broncos were helpless before the Roosters onslaught.  (Getty Images: Cameron Spencer)

When she started playing for Queensland and Australia in 2009 her Broncos teammate Reegan Hicks was three years old.

Club football was ad hoc, pathways barely existed and the NRL may as well have been a different universe. For the committed few who kept the women's game going it was day-to-day as much as it was hand-to-mouth.

Interstate matches were not played under the State of Origin banner and were held at suburban grounds in front of tiny crowds.

A World Cup final was the only game that could get on television and even then, only if the network was feeling generous.

Footage of those days leading up to the first NRLW season in 2018 is grainy and hard to find. Even basic details of matches — things like team lists, scorers and attendances — aren't always easy to track down.

Brigginshaw has been a top-level footballer for almost as long as some of her teammates have been alive.  (Getty Images: Mark Nolan)

In a very literal sense of the word, it's almost prehistoric.

Today it's a new world, a world Brigginshaw helped create as the premiere footballer and one of the biggest stars of the transitional era and into the early NRLW years.

For proof, look no further than the words of Julia Robinson, who has played with Brigginshaw ever since that first Broncos season.

“She’s a true leader, on and off the field, she’s the heart of the Broncos, she’s going to be this legacy that carries on for generations," Robinson told ABC Sport.
